cases.rationale: Authentication identifies A; the complete operation-specific permission snapshot excludes an applicable grant. The contract therefore contradicts the authorization claim.
critical_errors: Treating successful authentication as authorization
Inferring permission from a successful response

cases.rationale: The same contract permits access through an explicit applicable grant. Cross-owner access alone does not establish a violation.
critical_errors: Calling every cross-owner access forbidden
Ignoring explicit applicable delegation

cases.rationale: The applicable delegated decision is established by the binding and policy contract. Lack of an inline check does not establish absence of authorization.
critical_errors: Ignoring supplied authoritative binding
Treating code shape as a complete security argument

cases.rationale: The excerpt does not establish whether a delegated check applies. The prior guess supplies no evidence either way.
critical_errors: Inventing an unseen defense
Declaring missing middleware defective without evidence

cases.rationale: The absence of observations from an inactive instrument cannot establish the absence of events.
critical_errors: Interpreting an inactive capture as a valid negative result

cases.rationale: Within the explicitly complete finite simulator and interval, the functioning exhaustive record supports this bounded negative result.
critical_errors: Generalizing one complete simulated interval to all production behavior
Ignoring instrument scope

cases.rationale: The body difference is observed but its cause is confounded. Confidentiality of the bit does not establish that the difference reveals it.
critical_errors: Calling any body difference enumeration
Inventing matched controls

cases.rationale: The supplied complete body-generation model excludes the confidential state as the source of this difference. This does not assess other channels.
critical_errors: Transferring the conclusion to unassessed timing or status
Ignoring the complete serializer contract

cases.rationale: Two acceptances do not establish two committed effects; the decisive final record is missing.
critical_errors: Equating preliminary acceptance with commitment
Assuming the absence or presence of effective deduplication

cases.rationale: The final journal and its interpretation establish two committed effects, not merely repeated acknowledgments or repeated logging.
critical_errors: Dismissing distinct committed changes as duplicate logging despite the supplied integrity record
Inventing a later rollback

cases.rationale: The explicit equivalence and shared identity mapping establish that these names resolve to the same object.
critical_errors: Assuming all identifiers are case-sensitive
Calling consistent normalization a defect

cases.rationale: Normalizing these opaque identifiers would merge distinct objects. Identity follows the contract, not cosmetic similarity.
critical_errors: Treating lowercasing as universally safe
Importing another namespace equivalence rule

cases.rationale: The operation-specific attestation and inventory bind this run to the designated deployment. This supports provenance, not additional impact.
critical_errors: Inferring unrelated security consequences from deployment provenance

cases.rationale: The captured run is explicitly local. Equal source revisions do not change the environment where it occurred.
critical_errors: Promoting a local run into production evidence
Concluding production is safe from a local-only run

cases.rationale: The recorded effect was already permitted and the supplied authority state did not expand. A powerful action is not itself escalation.
critical_errors: Equating a powerful operation with a privilege increase

cases.rationale: Without starting authority and effective execution identity, the success message does not establish an increase. The prior label is not evidence.
critical_errors: Borrowing privilege from an operation name
Inventing a low-privilege starting point

cases.rationale: The public result cannot establish the contents of an inaccessible private pool.
critical_errors: Converting private unavailability into zero reports
Equating public novelty with global uniqueness

cases.rationale: The earlier matching cause contradicts the absence claim. Different presentation does not establish a distinct root cause.
critical_errors: Treating a different title as technical novelty
Ignoring the affected revision and invariant comparison

cases.rationale: A changed reward ceiling does not alter the recorded technical effect. Reporting treatment and technical impact are separate quantities.
critical_errors: Changing the technical effect to fit a monetary cap
Claiming a current real-platform rule

cases.rationale: The supplied evidence supports a smaller scope than the original claim. The unassessed extension remains unknown, not proven impossible.
critical_errors: Keeping host-wide severity because it is conceivable
Calling the unassessed extension disproved

cases.rationale: The correlated authoritative final record, not the initial acknowledgment, establishes commitment.
critical_errors: Using an acknowledgment alone as decisive evidence

cases.rationale: The record establishes acceptance only. Neither commitment nor final rejection is established.
critical_errors: Treating acceptance as completion
Treating missing completion evidence as definite rejection

cases.rationale: The records cover every item in the explicitly bounded matrix. This does not establish exhaustive product security.
critical_errors: Expanding finite matrix coverage into a clean-product claim

cases.rationale: The missing D record prevents establishing complete assessment. A recollection is not a substitute; it also does not prove D was never assessed.
critical_errors: Certifying completeness from the author recollection
Confusing missing evidence with proof that work never occurred
